# attestation-issuer

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from servlets/attestation-issuer/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/attestation-issuer.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `attestation-issuer` component of `servlets/attestation-issuer`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.servlet.attestation`: generated from its catalogue, attestation-issuer.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_ATTESTER_`, `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_`, `OIDF_WALLET_`, `OIDF_ENTRA_`, `OIDF_CIMD_`, `OIDF_AGENT_REGISTRY_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_ISSUER` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `challengeRequired` (init-param) | `false` | Whether an instance-key proof must carry a challenge from /federation/attestation/challenge; the issuance servlet enforces it, and from 0.8.0 the two discovery documents advertise the issuance servlet's value once it has started (each discovery servlet's own init-param answers only before then) | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false, in any case: the servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and its path answers 503 (under development yes, no, 1, 0, on and off are read as false, with a warning naming the strict spelling); before 0.6.0 anything but true meant false. Before 0.8.0 servlets given different values advertised one thing and enforced another | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_REQUIRED` (init-param `customClaimsRequired`, then system property `oidf.attestation.custom.claims.required`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_REQUIRED`) | Unset; a list | Claims every instance-key proof must carry besides the protocol's, comma-separated: enforced by the issuance servlet and advertised as custom_claims_required, from 0.8.0 as the issuance servlet read it once it has started; the init-param customClaimsRequired on a servlet wins over the system property and the environment | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Split at commas and spaces from 0.6.0 (at commas only before); a claim a client does not send refuses its every issuance | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_SUPPORTED` (init-param `customClaimsSupported`, then system property `oidf.attestation.custom.claims.supported`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_SUPPORTED`) | Unset; a list | Claims the client attestation service document advertises as custom_claims_supported, comma-separated; advertised only; the init-param customClaimsSupported on the metadata servlet wins over the system property and the environment | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (the metadata servlet's alone before 0.8.0). Split at commas and spaces from 0.6.0 (at commas only before); nothing enforces it | Any | No |
| `challengeEndpointEnabled` (init-param) | `true` | Whether the attester's challenge endpoint (/federation/attestation/challenge) serves and both discovery documents advertise it as challenge_endpoint; false answers 404 there (from 0.8.0; before, it only took challenge_endpoint out of the client attestation service document). The issuance servlet's value governs once it has started; each other servlet's own init-param answers only before then | **Doesn't start**: Set to anything but true or false, in any case: the part of the servlet it is set on (issuance, metadata, configuration or challenge) is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (under development yes, no, 1, 0, on and off are read as false, with a warning naming the strict spelling); before 0.6.0 anything but true meant false | Any | No |
| `attestationSigningAlgValuesSupported` (init-param) | Unset; a list | The algorithms attestations are signed with, comma-separated. Unset, they are the configured signing keys' algorithms (OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS and OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF, as the vault describes them): both the client attestation service document and /.well-known/client-attester advertise those as attestation_signing_alg_values_supported, and under the production profile the issuance servlet refuses to mint with any other key (server_error). Set, it narrows that list: it is advertised as written, and the issuance servlet refuses to mint with a key whose algorithm it does not list (server_error), in every profile. The issuance servlet's value governs; before it has started, neither document names an algorithm (from 0.8.0; before, the default RS256,PS256,ES256 was advertised only, from the metadata servlet, and /.well-known/client-attester named every asymmetric algorithm) | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the part of the servlet it is set on (issuance or metadata) is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (before 0.6.0 it meant the default). Split at commas and spaces. Set without the attester key's algorithm, every issuance for the clients that key signs for is refused, 500 server_error naming the setting; unset, nothing changes for a deployment's own keys | Any | Yes |
| `openBaoUrl` (init-param) | Unset | OpenBao's address for attestation signing keys (a client's attestation_signing_key_ref), on the issuance servlet; used only with openBaoToken, and with either unset both come from OIDF_OPENBAO_URL and OIDF_OPENBAO_TOKEN and their fallbacks (hosted-entity-signing) | **Per request**: Wrong or unreachable: a client whose attestation_signing_key_ref needs the vault is refused with server_error | Any | Yes |
| `openBaoToken` (init-param) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The OpenBao token for the same, on the issuance servlet; used only with openBaoUrl | **Per request**: Refused by OpenBao: as for openBaoUrl | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_FEDERATION_ENTITY` (system property `oidf.attester.federation.entity`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_FEDERATION_ENTITY`) | Unset; an http or https URL | An OpenID Federation entity whose signed statement maps SPIFFE IDs to clients, consulted before the CIMD clients and PingFederate's client store, and trusted only through a chain to a pinned trust anchor (OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_ANCHOR_JWKS); an entity the anchor stops vouching for loses its clients within 300 s | **First request**: Named with no trust anchor pinned, or not an http or https URL with a host: the attester refuses to build its client sources at its first request, so each issuance and each request for its configuration documents answers 500 server_error, and server.log names it under the response's correlation id | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK` (system property `oidf.attester.signing.jwk`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK`) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The attester's private signing key as an inline JWK, applied to every client the federation entity or the CIMD document describes when OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF is unset; development only (X-B04, F-0626): production signs with OpenBao transit keys, so the private key never enters PingFederate | **Doesn't start**: Set in production: the start-up audit refuses ATTESTATION_ISSUER, naming it; move the key to OpenBao and set OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF. Missing or malformed in development: those clients are refused (invalid_client) at issuance | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS` (system property `oidf.attester.signing.keys`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS`) | Unset; a JSON object | The OpenBao transit keys the attester may sign with, and the issuers each signs for: a JSON object of key name to {"issuers": ["https://attester.example.com"]} (X-B04, F-0625). A client's attestation_signing_key_ref, and OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF, must be a member whose issuers include the client's attestation_issuer. Required in production for any client that names a key ref; unset in development, any key ref is allowed with a warning. Give the attester's OpenBao token a policy allowing transit/sign on these keys only | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object of OpenBao key names to {"issuers": [https URLs]}: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Unset in production: every client that names a key ref is refused (invalid_client), and the AttesterSigningKeys part is DEGRADED. A key or issuer missing: that client is refused (invalid_client, attestation.issuer.signing_key_refused) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF` (system property `oidf.attester.signing.key.ref`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REF`) | Unset | The OpenBao transit key the attester signs federation and CIMD clients with (X-B04); a federation entry may not name a key of its own. Replaces OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK in production; must be listed in OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS for each such client's issuer | **Doesn't start**: Not an OpenBao transit key name: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. A key the vault cannot describe: the AttesterSigningKeys part is DEGRADED and those clients' issuance answers server_error. Unset with no OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK: those clients are refused (invalid_client) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REFRESH_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.attester.signing.key.refresh.seconds`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEY_REFRESH_SECONDS`) | `300`; seconds, 60 to 86400 | How often, in seconds, the attester reads each OpenBao transit key it signs with again (X-B04, F-0627): a key rotated in OpenBao signs, with a new kid, within this time and without a restart. The keys published in OIDF_FEDERATION_ATTESTER_JWKS are read at start, so rotate a federation-published attester with a new key name (the attester README's rotation runbook). A re-read that fails keeps the version read before, with a warning, and is tried again within a minute | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 60 to 86400: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS` (system property `oidf.cimd.clients`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS`) | Unset; a JSON object | The attester's CIMD clients, a JSON object keyed by each client's Client Identifier URL (https, a path, no userinfo, query, fragment or dot segment; compared as written): each member's issuer (required), evidence_type (default spiffe-jwt), trust_root (a member of OIDF_CIMD_TRUST_BUNDLES; required unless the evidence type needs no trust bundle), subject_prefixes (required: every instance subject the client's document lists must start with one), max_issued_ttl (seconds, 1-64800, default 300) and signing_key_ref. The attester fetches one Client ID Metadata Document per client from its URL and takes only the instances, their entitlements and metadata, the client-level entitlement and an issued_ttl from its oauth_client_attestation member (CAS §6.1); a document that names a trust root, an issuer or a key is refused (CAS §6.2 rule 3). Listed, the client attestation service document lists cimd in client_metadata_sources_supported | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object, a key that is not a Client Identifier URL, an unknown member, a missing issuer, trust_root or subject_prefixes, a trust_root that names no trust root (or one with no trust_domain where the evidence type needs one), or an unsupported evidence type: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, the client URL and the member, never a value | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CIMD_TRUST_BUNDLES` (system property `oidf.cimd.trust.bundles`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_TRUST_BUNDLES`) | Unset; a JSON object | The trust roots CIMD clients' instance attestations are checked against, the operator's own and never a document's (CAS §6.2 rule 3): a JSON object of a name of your choosing to a root with exactly one of jwks (a JWK Set of public keys) and jwks_uri (an https URL, fetched through the outbound rules with no exemption), and trust_domain (needed for spiffe-jwt) or evidence_issuer. OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS names a root with trust_root | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object, a root that is not an object, an unknown member, both or neither of jwks and jwks_uri, a JWK Set that cannot be read or holds a private key member, or a jwks_uri that is not https: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting and the root, never a value | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_EXTERNAL_CEILINGS` (system property `oidf.attester.external.ceilings`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_EXTERNAL_CEILINGS`) | Unset; a JSON object | The attester's cap on what a client from an external source - an OpenID Federation entity (OIDF_ATTESTER_FEDERATION_ENTITY) or a CIMD client (OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS) - may be granted: a JSON object of client id to an authorization_details array, with "*" as the cap for any external client not named (a named entry wins). Every ceiling the source declares, client-level and per instance, is narrowed to its meet with the cap (CAS §7 rule 4: policy may further constrain, never widen), and a source that declares no ceiling still grants nothing. PingFederate-store clients are never capped. In production an external client with no entry and no "*" is refused (invalid_client); in development it stands uncapped with a WARN | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object, an empty client id, or an array the RAR containment models refuse (a type with no model, an undeclared field, a value its rule cannot compare): the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting and the client id, never a value. Unset in production while a federation entity or CIMD clients are configured: every one of those clients is refused, logged and evented as attestation.issuer.client_refused (no_external_ceiling) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CIMD_REFRESH_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.cimd.refresh.seconds`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_REFRESH_SECONDS`) | `300`; seconds, 60 to 3600 | How often, in seconds, the attester fetches each CIMD client's document again, on a background thread; sooner when the response's Cache-Control max-age is lower, never more often than every 60 s | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 60 to 3600: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting | Any | No |
| `OIDF_CIMD_MAX_STALE_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.cimd.max.stale.seconds`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_MAX_STALE_SECONDS`) | `3600`; seconds, 60 to 86400 | How long, in seconds after it was fetched, a CIMD client's last good document is served while fetching it fails (a transport error, a status other than 200, a body over the cap); then the client is dropped until a fetch succeeds. A document that fetches but is refused drops its client at once | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 60 to 86400, or less than OIDF_CIMD_REFRESH_SECONDS: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_CIMD_MAX_BYTES` (system property `oidf.cimd.max.bytes`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_MAX_BYTES`) | `5120`; a whole number, 1024 to 65536 | The most bytes of a CIMD client's document the attester reads (5 KiB by default, as the CIMD draft recommends, up to 64 KiB); a longer body is an error, and the last good document is kept | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1024 to 65536: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_OP_ISSUER` (system property `oidf.attester.op.issuer`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_OP_ISSUER`) | Unset | The hosted attester's own entity id, the relying party in a wallet provider's trust chain; with a trust controller configured (OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_CONTROLLER_HOST) it turns on federation-backed wallet provider trust, in preference to OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS | **Per request**: Wrong: no wallet provider's chain resolves, and every wallet instance attestation is refused. Read at deploy as well as at the first request, like the attester's other settings | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS` (system property `oidf.wallet.provider.jwks`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS`) | Unset; a JSON object | Wallet providers trusted statically, development only: a JSON object of provider entity id to its JWK Set of public keys, used only when federation-backed wallet trust is not configured; the keys are trusted with no trust chain | **Doesn't start**: Set in production: the start-up audit refuses ATTESTATION_ISSUER, naming it (from 0.8.0, F-0632). Not a JSON object, or an entry that is not a JWK Set of public keys: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (before 0.8.0 such an entry was skipped without a word), and the metadata servlet's too when it is not a JSON object | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_ATTESTATION_TYPES` (system property `oidf.wallet.attestation.types`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_ATTESTATION_TYPES`) | `oauth-client-attestation+jwt`; a list | The typ header values a wallet instance attestation may carry, comma-separated; a WIA with no typ, or another one, is refused. The default is the one draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth-11 section 4 names; before 0.8.0 a missing typ and three unregistered wallet types were accepted | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Missing a type a wallet provider uses: every WIA it issues is refused as invalid_instance_attestation, counted under check=typ | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_ATTESTATION_AUD_REQUIRED` (system property `oidf.wallet.attestation.aud.required`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_ATTESTATION_AUD_REQUIRED`) | `true` | Whether a wallet instance attestation must carry an aud naming this attester. HAIP 1.0 wallet attestations carry none; with false such a WIA is accepted, one that has an aud must still name this attester, and the evidence binding (the first presenter of a WIA wins it, with its key and client) is then the only replay control | **Per request**: true with HAIP wallets: every WIA without an aud is refused as invalid_instance_attestation, counted under check=aud. Not true or false: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming it | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_REQUIRED_PROVIDERS` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.required.providers`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_REQUIRED_PROVIDERS`) | Unset; a list | The wallet providers, by entity id, whose wallet instance attestations must carry a status claim pointing to a Token Status List (draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21), comma-separated, or * for every provider; unset, a WIA without status is accepted and one with status is checked either way | **Per request**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. A provider listed whose WIAs carry no status: each is refused as invalid_instance_attestation, audited as attestation.evidence.status_refused with reason status_required. A provider left out: a WIA it issues without status is accepted, and revoking it is not seen until it expires | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_BYTES` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.max.bytes`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_BYTES`) | `1048576`; a whole number, 1024 to 16777216 | The largest Status List Token response body, in bytes, the attester reads when it fetches a wallet attestation's status list (1 MiB by default, 1 KiB to 16 MiB); a larger body is refused unread past the limit | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 1024 to 16777216: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Too small for a provider's list: every WIA pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable, counted as oidf_attester_wallet_status_fetches_total{result=too_large} | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.max.list.bytes`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES`) | `16777216`; a whole number, 1024 to 134217728 | The largest inflated Status List, in bytes, the attester decompresses (16 MiB by default, 1 KiB to 128 MiB): decompression stops once the output passes it, so a compressed bomb costs at most this much memory per fetch | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 1024 to 134217728: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Too small for a provider's list: every WIA pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable, counted under result=invalid | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MIN` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.ttl.min`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MIN`) | `60`; seconds, 0 to 3600 | The shortest time, in seconds, a fetched Status List Token is trusted before it is fetched again, whatever smaller ttl it carries (draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21 section 11.5); its exp still ends it sooner | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 0 to 3600, or above OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MAX: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Too large: a revocation is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MAX` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.ttl.max`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MAX`) | `3600`; seconds, 60 to 86400 | The longest time, in seconds, a fetched Status List Token is trusted before it is fetched again, whatever larger ttl it carries, and the time a token with no ttl is trusted; its exp still ends it sooner | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 60 to 86400, or below OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_TTL_MIN: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Too large: a revocation is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_STALE_GRACE` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.stale.grace`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_STALE_GRACE`) | `0`; seconds, 0 to 900 | How long, in seconds, a Status List Token past its freshness stays usable while it cannot be fetched again (0 by default, at most 900), never past its exp; after that a WIA pointing to it is answered 503 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 0 to 900: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Above 0: a revocation published while the list host is unreachable is seen up to this much later | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (system property `oidf.wallet.status.cache.max.bytes`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`) | `67108864`; a whole number, 1048576 to 1073741824 | The most inflated Status List bytes, in all, each node keeps in its cache of wallet attestations' status lists (64 MiB by default, 1 MiB to 1 GiB, and never below OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES); past it the least recently used lists are dropped and fetched again when next needed | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 1048576 to 1073741824, or below OIDF_WALLET_STATUS_MAX_LIST_BYTES: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Too small for the lists in use: they are fetched again more often, each fetch counted in oidf_attester_wallet_status_fetches_total. Too large: a wallet provider's many large lists can hold that much heap on every node | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ENTRA_AGENT_DIRECTORY` (system property `oidf.entra.agent.directory`, then env `OIDF_ENTRA_AGENT_DIRECTORY`) | Unset; a JSON object | The Entra Agent ID directory, a JSON object of asserted oid to directory entry (display_name, groups, ceiling, tenant, evidence_types, instances), which registers the entra-directory asserted-context resolver; an entry is resolved only for evidence of its evidence_types (default azure-mi-token and aks-sa-token) from its tenant and its instances (instances required under the production profile), and its ceiling only narrows an evidenced one | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object, an entry that is not an object or carries an unknown member, a blank oid, a display_name that is not a string, groups, evidence_types or instances that are not lists of strings, a tenant that is not a GUID, or a ceiling the containment models refuse; or, under the production profile, an entry with no tenant or no instances: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting and the entry (before 0.8.0 a directory that could not be read, and any entry that was not an object, was dropped without a word) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL` (system property `oidf.attester.spire.reader.url`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL`) | Unset; an https URL | The SPIRE entry reader's https base URL (services/spire-entry-reader); set, the attester reads the registration entries of each verified spiffe-jwt SPIFFE ID in OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_TRUST_DOMAIN over mutual TLS and adds the spire: selectors every entry shares to the identity's evidence selectors; unset, SPIRE is never asked | **Doesn't start**: Not an https URL with a host: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Unreachable: OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_FAILURE_MODE decides, refusing each spiffe-jwt issuance (closed) or issuing without spire: selectors (downscope) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_TRUST_DOMAIN` (system property `oidf.attester.spire.reader.trust.domain`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_TRUST_DOMAIN`) | Unset | The SPIFFE trust domain the SPIRE reader serves; required with OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL. Every spiffe-jwt instance is read; one whose SPIFFE ID is outside it is refused (403 instance_not_authorized) without a request, in either failure mode. The cloud evidence types are never read | **Doesn't start**: Unset with the URL, or not lower-case letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_': FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Another domain than the reader's: every spiffe-jwt issuance is refused as wrong_domain | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_CA_FILE` (system property `oidf.attester.spire.reader.ca.file`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_CA_FILE`) | Unset; a file path | A PEM file of the certificate authorities that issue the SPIRE reader's server certificate; required with OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL. It is the reader client's only trust: not PingFederate's trusted CAs, not the JVM's. The server certificate must also name the URL's host | **Doesn't start**: Unset with the URL, unreadable, or holding no certificate: FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. The wrong authority: every read fails as tls | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_CLIENT_KEY_PAIR` (system property `oidf.attester.spire.reader.client.key.pair`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_CLIENT_KEY_PAIR`) | Unset | The alias of the PingFederate SSL client key pair (Security, SSL Client Keys and Certificates) the attester presents to the SPIRE reader; required with OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL. The reader pins its public key. Read again at most every 60 s, so a rotated key pair needs no restart | **Doesn't start**: Unset with the URL: FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. No such key pair: FAILED_CONFIG in production; in development a WARN, and every read fails as tls until it exists | Any | Yes |

## Removed

Still set in the source it was read from, a removed name is refused, naming what replaces it - unless its row says Ignored: a plugin's field whose stored value the plugin ignores, so a configuration saved before the release still imports and the plugin still runs.

| Setting | Read from | Instead | Removed in | When still set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_CIMD_URL` | env | `OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS` | 0.8.0 | Refused |
| `oidf.attester.cimd.url` | system property | `OIDF_CIMD_CLIENTS` | 0.8.0 | Refused |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_ENTRIES_URL` | env | `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL` | 0.8.0 | Refused |
| `oidf.attester.spire.entries.url` | system property | `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_READER_URL` | 0.8.0 | Refused |
